Saadia-specific moves preserved per data-source/saadia-gloss-table.json; Blau's notes (data-source/blau-genesis-notes.json) consulted for Bereshit 1-12.

translations.1: Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses on account of the fair woman whom he had married, for he had kept himself apart from her.
translations.2: And they said: 'If it be on account of prophecy — was it only he alone whom God addressed? Has God not addressed us as well?' And God heard that.
translations.3: Now Moses was a man exceedingly humble — more than all the people who are upon the face of the earth.
translations.4: And God said suddenly to Moses and Aaron and Miriam: 'Come out, the three of you, to the tent of the assembly.' And the three of them came out.
translations.5: And God appeared in a pillar of cloud, and stood at the door of the tent, and called: 'O Aaron, and O Miriam!' And the two of them came out.
translations.6: He said: 'Hear my words. If there be a prophet among you — I, God, make Myself known to him in a vision, or I speak to him in a dream.
translations.7: Not so My servant Moses — rather, throughout all My nation he is trusted.
translations.8: Mouth to mouth I address him, and by vision and not in riddles; and the created forms of God appointed for him — he beholds them. Why then were the two of you not afraid to speak against My servant Moses?'
translations.9: And God's anger intensified against them, and His light ascended.
translations.10: And as the cloud withdrew from the tent, behold — Miriam was white as snow. And when Aaron turned toward Miriam, behold, she was stricken with a skin-affliction.
translations.11: And Aaron said to Moses: 'O my lord, do not lay a sin upon us for what we did in our ignorance and in our error.
translations.12: Let her not be like a stillborn that comes out from its mother's womb with half its body already wasted away.'
translations.13: And Moses cried out to his Lord, saying: 'O God, heal her, I pray!'
translations.14: And God said to Moses: 'Were her father to spit in her face, would she not be obliged to feel shame before him for seven days? Let her remain thus outside the camp, and after that she shall rejoin it.'
translations.15: And Miriam remained outside the camp for seven days; and the people did not set out until she had rejoined.
translations.16: And after that they set out from Hazeroth, and encamped in the wilderness of Paran.
